title: Renaming Columns & Indexes 🏷️
description: Give your columns meaningful names and manage row labels with ease.

slides.title: Why Names Matter 🏷️
slides.content:
# Clear Metadata = Understandable Data

Columns with spaces, special characters, or cryptic abbreviations make analysis painful. Renaming and setting a proper index improve readability and efficiency.

slides.title: Example DataFrame
slides.codeSnippet:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'First Name': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie'],
    'Last Name': ['Smith', 'Jones', 'Brown'],
    'Age (Years)': [25, 30, 35]
})
print(df)

slides.title: Renaming Columns ✏️
slides.content:
## `rename()`

Use `rename()` with a dictionary mapping old names to new ones:

```python
df.rename(columns={'First Name': 'first_name', 'Last Name': 'last_name'})
```

- `inplace=True` modifies the DataFrame directly.
- You can also rename indexes with `rename(index={'old':'new'})`.

To rename all columns at once, assign a list to `df.columns`:
```python
df.columns = ['first_name', 'last_name', 'age']
```

slides.title: Rename Columns
slides.codeSnippet:
df = df.rename(columns={
    'First Name': 'first_name',
    'Last Name': 'last_name',
    'Age (Years)': 'age'
})
print(df.columns.tolist())
print(df.head())

quizData.question: What does `df.rename(columns={'A':'B'}, inplace=True)` do?

options.text: Returns a new DataFrame with column 'A' renamed to 'B'
Modifies the original DataFrame in place

quizData.explanation: With `inplace=True`, the operation is performed on the same DataFrame.

slides.title: Setting a Column as Index 🎯
slides.content:
## `set_index()`

Moves a column to become the row index:

```python
df.set_index('first_name', inplace=True)
```

- The old index is discarded.
- To keep the column as well, use `drop=False`.

This is common for ID columns or unique identifiers.

quizData.question: After `df.set_index('col')`, what happens to the previous index?

options.text: It merges with the new index
It stays as the index alongside

quizData.explanation: By default, `set_index()` replaces the index entirely.

slides.title: Resetting the Index ↩️
slides.content:
## `reset_index()`

Moves the current index back to a column and creates a default integer index:

```python
df.reset_index(inplace=True)
```

- `drop=True` avoids keeping the old index as a column.
- Useful after filtering/dropping rows to clean up indices.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Rename with a Function

You can use a function to transform all column names: `df.rename(columns=str.lower, inplace=True)` makes everything lowercase.

slides.title: Index & Rename Practice 🏋️
slides.content:
1. Create a DataFrame with columns: 'Product ID', 'Product Name', 'Price ($)'.
2. Rename columns to lower_snake_case (e.g., 'product_id', 'product_name', 'price').
3. Set 'product_id' as the index.
4. Reset the index but keep the old index as a column.
5. Print the final DataFrame.

slides.title: Metadata Polished 🎉
slides.content: Column names and indexes are now tidy. Finally, we’ll handle extreme values.
